Maya: ran a bounded-prefetch-window sweep across h100-us-west and a100-eu with a heavy long-tail slen mix. quick summary: small window (<=32) drops p99 on H100 but hitrate falls; large window helps hitrate but increases average latency. attaching fast numbers below :chart_with_upwards_trend:

Maya: config snippet:
```
prefetch_window: 32
eviction: lru+age
region: us-west-2 (h100)
slen_mix: {1:0.6, 64:0.25, 1024:0.15}
model: redwood-v1-7b-ql4
```

Maya: results (h100, prefetch=32):
```
p50: 7.9ms  p95: 26.3ms  p99: 82.1ms  hitrate: 76.8%  tokens/sec: 11.3k
```

Maya: results (a100, prefetch=128):
```
p50: 9.8ms  p95: 34.1ms  p99: 140.9ms  hitrate: 88.5%  tokens/sec: 9.6k
```

Cheng: nice, can you drop the raw traces? want the tail-cause (paging vs kernel stalls).

Maya: uploaded traces and summary csv to gs://redwood-bench/prefetch/bounded/1901234567/summary.csv (public to internal). also a short perf plot: https://app.fig/links/bench-1901234567

Sam: did you run quantized model variants (4bit/8bit)? curious if cache behavior changes with kernel choice.

Maya: yes — 4bit ql4 on H100: hitrate ~75%, p99 slightly higher (~95ms) vs fp16. on A100 the 4bit kernel adds ~10-15ms p50 but hitrate pattern similar.

Anya: is there an obvious sweet spot for window size by seqlen bucket? i.e. small window for short requests, larger for long ones?

Maya: we tried a simple heuristic: window = min(128, max(8, seqlen/8)) — improved overall latency by ~6% and kept hitrate within 3% of the static-large-window baseline. will push config later.

Cheng: can you paste the simple script you used to map seqlen->window?

Maya: snippet:
```python
def window_for_seqlen(seqlen):
    return min(128, max(8, seqlen // 8))
```

Maya: quick table (aggregated):
```
policy, p99(h100), hitrate
static-32, 82ms, 77%
static-128, 120ms, 89%
adaptive, 78ms, 86%
```

perf-bot: job/bench.prefetch.1901234567 finished in 12m 42s — artifacts uploaded.

Sam: ok cool. next step: run canary on a dedicated pool (small % of prod traffic) with adaptive window + aggressive eviction when mem pressure >80%. want to see real-world effect.

Cheng: +1. also add kernel-tagging so runtime prefers H100 optimized kernels for high-slen streams.

Anya: i'll draft a short rollout plan. propose 2% traffic, monitor p99, error-rate, and hitrate per-customer. rollback threshold p99 +25% or hitrate drop >10%.

Maya: i'll schedule the canary and post results here. thanks all :thumbsup:
